display_conformance.display: dcmtk agrees on 1,000 of 1,020 grayscale renderings (within 1 grey level)
display_conformance.source: /media/barracuda/shlink-display-conformance/out/report.json (UNTRACKED scratch, 15 Oct 16:49) produced by web/checks/display-conformance.ts + .py; summarized in commit fef0a72's message
display_conformance.quote: - display-conformance: 1,328 grayscale files; dcmtk agrees on 1,000 of 1,020, pydicom on 779 of 790, every difference triaged
display_conformance.how: recomputed from report.json with the script's own rule (max diff <= 1 grey level): dcmtk compared 1020, agree 1000 (facts_cmds.sh §3)
display_conformance.note: Triage of the 20 is NOT written up in the repo (only 'every difference triaged' in the commit message); categories below are my reconstruction from report.json: 9 = our deliberate VOI LUT bit-depth rule (6 of Josh's CR hand views + 1 IDC RF + 2 synthetic edge cases; dcmtk takes the declared 16 bits and washes the image out — this is the Josh 'Hand OBLI shows white' bug); 8 = files with no window, rendered by min-max where auto-window choices differ (5 GE PET, Cornell JPEG, GE DLX private syntax, Siemens GBS III; no pydicom reference for these); 2 = within 2 grey levels on >=99.9% of pixels; 1 = Orthanc MalaterreCP246 JPEG-LS, where pydicom matches ours exactly and only dcmtk differs. What the 1,328 files are: 531 IDC files (objects cache), 500 real codec-corpus files, 277 corpus files from synthetic seeds, 9 of Josh's sample originals, 11 synthetic LUT edge cases. Of the 1,020 dcmtk comparisons, 135 involve synthetic pixels (124 corpus-synthetic + 11 edge cases); REAL-ONLY dcmtk agreement = 867 of 885. pydicom: 779/790.

value: I don't love optionality here, how does a client even know what's deflated.
Final record delimiter… why is that needed? Doesn't ending at that point also accomplish the same?
Why use HKDF at that point?
design_questions.display: 4 questions → no ZIP, no optional deflate, no final-record delimiter, no HKDF
design_questions.quote: - **"What's the zip buying us?"** Nothing the offsets in the `ImagingStudy` and the GCM tags didn't already provide, so the encrypted files became the DICOM instances laid end to end.
design_questions.note: Effects: (1) ZIP dropped: encrypted files are the DICOM instances laid end to end; offsets in ImagingStudy + GCM tags suffice. (2) Optional compression dropped: image compression lives inside DICOM; one client code path. (3) Final-record delimiter dropped: the authenticated Bundle gives each instance's length, so truncation is detectable. (4) HKDF dropped: each file has its own random key inside the link's Bundle. (A fifth question in the same section removed the slide-offset Bundle extension: 'Is this suggestion only to rescue slides that lack metadata that could be present in DICOM?') Q2 also appears in docs/PROCESS-NOTES.md:50.
